# The coded values a rule records that a sentence shows as a localized label:
# the rule, the context field the code is read from, the placeholder the label
# is written to, and the string-resource map it is looked up in. The formatter
# adds these placeholders to a finding's values, and the setup's placeholder
# check accepts them beside the fields the rule records.
context_decorations <- tibble::tribble(
  ~rule_id, ~field,           ~placeholder,    ~labels,
  19L,      "infection_type", "ssi_type",      "ssi_types",
  47L,      "type",           "type_label",    "admission_types",
  50L,      "device",         "device_label",  "devices",
  51L,      "count",          "count_label",   "day_counts",
  55L,      "sec_bsi",        "sec_bsi_label", "secondary_bsi_items"
)
# The maps the decorations look their labels up in, under the names the table
# above gives them. They are listed one by one as literal `sR$key` references:
# the string-layer check reads those to tell a live key from a dead one, and a
# map reached by a name taken from the table would count as unused. The
# devices take the glossary's abbreviations, which the forms use as well.
label_maps <- function(sR) list(
  ssi_types           = sR$ssi_types,
  admission_types     = sR$admission_types,
  devices             = list(cvc = sR$cvc, pvc = sR$pvc, niv = sR$niv, inv = sR$inv),
  day_counts          = sR$day_counts,
  secondary_bsi_items = sR$secondary_bsi_items)

# The fields a rule records twice, as a name and as the code it names: where
# the name is missing, as it is for a code the option set does not carry, the
# formatter shows the code the record holds in its place. The setup checks
# that both fields are ones the rule records.
context_fallbacks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~rule_id, ~field,      ~fallback,
  52L,      "substance", "substance_code",
  53L,      "substance", "substance_code",
  54L,      "substance", "substance_code"
)

# The solutions a solution's text points at. A report that includes a
# solution has to include the ones it cites, or the reader meets a reference
# to a section that is not there. The references are Quarto cross-references
# (`@sec-solution-N`), which no R parser reads, so they are collected with a
# pattern; the ids are the same in every language, so the English sources are
# read whatever language is rendered.
solution_references <- function(ids) {
  if (length(ids) == 0L)
    return(integer())
  text <- vapply(
    paste0("en/_solution_", sprintf("%04d", ids), ".Rmd"),
    readr::read_file, character(1))
  refs <- unlist(regmatches(text, gregexpr("@sec-solution-[0-9]+", text)))
  unique(as.integer(sub("@sec-solution-", "", refs, fixed = TRUE)))
}

# `ids` together with every solution reachable from them through the
# references in their texts. An id the catalogue does not have is dropped,
# whether given or cited: the offline check in the workspace refuses it, and
# a render should not — it has no file to read for it.
close_solutions <- function(ids) {
  catalogued <- function(x) intersect(unique(as.integer(x)), solution_info$id)
  ids <- catalogued(ids)
  repeat {
    new_ids <- setdiff(catalogued(solution_references(ids)), ids)
    if (length(new_ids) == 0L)
      return(ids)
    ids <- c(ids, new_ids)
  }
}
